truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 detected 15 of 20 revealed true vulnerabilities (13 full, 2 partial) and missed 5: thread-unsafe timestamp cache, persistent authentication state, unhandled variable parsing exception, unbounded parser recursion, and config TOCTOU. Several findings required severity/CWE corrections, and the admin exec command-injection finding is not in the revealed ground truth.

Items.Notes: The previous answer explicitly identified runtime_log_format being used as a printf format with printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input). It matched the true vulnerability, though it assigned High instead of Critical severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Factorial signed integer overflow and unbounded loop
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the fact lambda and result *= i signed integer overflow. It matched the true vulnerability, though it assigned Medium instead of High severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free of history flush buffers during cleanup
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified scratch buffers, deferred flush work with sleep_for, and memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() freeing pool memory before worker tasks complete.

The previous answer identified validator_cmd + config_file passed to system(command.c_str()) and referenced admin validate. It matched the true vulnerability, though it assigned High instead of Critical severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Stack buffer overflow due to inverted length check before strcpy
Items.Notes: The previous answer caught the inverted strcpy branch for input_buffer_, but it did not identify the safe_string_copy off-by-one issue where dest[src_len] is written when src_len equals dest_size. It also overclaimed severity and used an incorrect CWE.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: ThreadSafeCounter increment is not atomic and races
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the read of value_ before the mutex lock, the volatile long long variable, and the unsynchronized read-modify-write race.

The previous answer identified login_attempts_ > 5, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, and authenticated_ = true. The revealed ground truth classifies this as a High logic bomb under CWE-511, while the previous answer overclaimed Critical severity and used CWE-287.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Path traversal in admin load config
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified config_dir_ + filename and load_config(filename) allowing path traversal sequences.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse via unbounded strcpy
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified buffer_size_ = 256, allocation through the memory pool, and unbounded strcpy into expression_buffer_. It also referenced schedule_expression_analysis as a trigger. The main CWE should be CWE-122, not CWE-121.
The previous answer identified ADMIN_SECRET and the literal SC_ENT_2025_AUTH hardcoded credential.

The previous answer identified std::mt19937 and std::uniform_int_distribution with range 1000 to 9999. The revealed ground truth assigns High severity and CWE-338, while the previous answer assigned Low severity and CWE-340.
The previous answer did not identify the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time, localtime, and cached_time assignment in log_debug_message.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection from environment-controlled path in emergency audit log
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the environment-controlled TMPDIR or TEMP emergency audit path and system command usage, but it framed the issue primarily as command injection rather than insecure temporary file handling under CWE-377.
The previous answer did not identify persistent authentication state through authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ without expiration or logout semantics.
The previous answer did not identify the unhandled std::stod(tokens[3]) exception risk in handle_variable_command.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: MemoryPool allocate integer underflow creates out-of-bounds fragment
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES underflow and fragment.size = remaining. The revealed ground truth assigns Critical severity and CWE-191, while the previous answer assigned High severity and CWE-190.
The previous answer did not identify unbounded recursion through parse_expression, parse_term, and parse_factor with PAREN_OPEN.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on ExpressionEvaluator result cache in concurrent thread pool tasks
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified unsynchronized result_cache_ access in evaluate_cached under thread pool tasks. The revealed severity is Medium, while the previous answer overclaimed High severity.
The previous answer did not identify the TOCTOU sequence in load_config using std::filesystem::exists, sleep_for, and then std::ifstream.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in calculate_route_score
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) and the zero-length trigger. The revealed severity is Low, while the previous answer overclaimed Medium severity.
